explain: Size, space inside (padding), a line around (border), space outside (margin).
example: Spacing out cards so they do not touch.

explain: Puts the children in a row with gaps between them, centered top to bottom.
example: A navigation bar with a logo and links.

explain: A grid of 3 equal columns. 1fr means one share of the free space.
example: A photo gallery.

explain: The font, its size, and the space between lines.
example: Making a long article easy to read.

explain: Text and background colors, and a different color while the mouse is over it.
example: Buttons that react when you point at them.

syntax:
.parent { position: relative; }
.badge  { position: absolute; top: 0; right: 0; }
explain: absolute places an element by its nearest parent that has position: relative.
example: A red notification count on the corner of an icon.

explain: Rules inside only apply on screens 600px wide or less.
example: One column on phones, three columns on laptops.

explain: Picks links inside .nav, but only while the mouse is over them.
example: Menu links that underline when you point at them.

explain: Select by tag name, by .class, or by #id.
example: Styling all paragraphs, some boxes, one heading.

syntax:
nav a { color: white; }
ul > li { list-style: none; }
explain: A space means "anywhere inside". > means "direct child only".
example: Links only inside the menu.

explain: A comma gives several selectors the same style.
example: All headings at once.

syntax:
input[type="email"] { border-color: blue; }
a[href^="https"] { color: green; }
explain: [attr="value"] selects by attribute. ^= means "starts with".
example: Styling only email inputs.

explain: Pick elements by their position. even/odd or 2n+1 also work.
example: Striped table rows.

explain: ::before and ::after add content before or after an element using CSS.
example: Icons and arrows without extra HTML.

explain: :focus is the box you're typing in, :disabled is a turned-off button, :not() excludes something.
example: Showing which field is active.

explain: * selects every element.
example: A reset at the top of a stylesheet.

explain: Shorthand: two values = top/bottom then left/right; four = top, right, bottom, left (clockwise).
example: Spacing around and inside boxes.

explain: margin: 0 auto centers a block that has a width. max-width stops it overflowing on phones.
example: A centered page column.

explain: border is width, style and color. border-radius rounds the corners.
example: Cards and buttons.

explain: min-height sets the smallest height. overflow: auto adds a scrollbar when content is too big.
example: A full-screen section, a scrolling list.

explain: block takes a full line, inline flows with text, inline-block flows but can have a width. none hides it.
example: Hiding a menu, sizing badges.

explain: justify-content spaces items along the row, align-items lines them up across it.
example: A header with logo left and menu right.

explain: flex-direction: column stacks items top to bottom. gap adds space between them.
example: A form with fields under each other.

explain: flex: 1 makes an item take the leftover space. flex-wrap lets items go to the next line.
example: A search box that fills the bar; tags that wrap.

explain: Makes as many 200px+ columns as fit. It changes by itself with the screen size.
example: A photo gallery that works on any screen.

explain: span 2 takes two columns. 1 / -1 goes from the first to the last column.
example: A big featured card in a grid.

explain: place-items: center puts the content in the exact middle.
example: Centering a login box on the screen.

syntax:
.top-bar { position: sticky; top: 0; }
.chat { position: fixed; bottom: 20px; right: 20px; }
explain: sticky stays on screen once you scroll to it. fixed always stays in the same spot on the screen.
example: Sticky headers, a chat button.

explain: z-index decides what is on top. Bigger numbers go in front.
example: Menus that cover the page.

explain: rem is relative to the html font size. line-height is the space between lines.
example: Easy-to-read text.

explain: Boldness, alignment, capital letters, and space between letters.
example: Small labels like "NEW".

explain: Load a font from Google Fonts, then use it. The second name is a backup.
example: Using a custom font.

explain: Keeps text on one line and adds "..." when it doesn't fit.
example: Long file names in a list.

explain: Four ways to write a color. The last number in rgba is see-through-ness (0 to 1).
example: Matching brand colors.

explain: A gradient fades from one color to another.
example: Colorful banners.

explain: box-shadow: x, y, blur, color. It makes the box look lifted.
example: Cards that float above the page.

explain: --name stores a value. var(--name) uses it. Change it once, it changes everywhere.
example: Theme colors.

explain: transition makes changes smooth instead of instant.
example: Buttons that fade when you hover.

explain: transform moves, grows, or turns an element without moving others.
example: A playful hover effect.

explain: @keyframes describes an animation; animation plays it.
example: A loading spinner.

explain: cursor changes the mouse pointer. opacity makes an element see-through.
example: Showing something is clickable or disabled.

explain: min-width rules apply on screens this wide or wider. Start with phones, add for big screens.
example: Mobile-first layouts.

explain: Images shrink to fit their box and keep their shape.
example: Photos that never overflow on phones.

explain: clamp(min, preferred, max). vw is 1% of the screen width.
example: Headings that grow with the screen.

explain: Applies when the computer is in dark mode.
example: Dark mode.

explain: calc() does math with units. aspect-ratio keeps a shape; object-fit: cover fills it without stretching.
example: Video thumbnails.
